moods.start: Heaven Hill, Cobble Lookout when stamina allows, Wilmington Town Beach, Adirondack Carousel.
Mount Jo, Copperas Pond, Mt Van Hoevenberg, Ausable Chasm or a boat day.
Cascade Lakes picnic, Jay Covered Bridge, a clear-day Whiteface drive, galleries and farm stores.
Olympic Museum, a confirmed public skate, Big Z's, a movie or The Wild Center.
Cascade, Jay Mountain or Giant; choose the route and weather conservatively.

dayPlans.name: Young family: stay close to Wilmington
dayPlans.plan: Choose Cobble Lookout only if the children are comfortable with two-plus trail miles; otherwise skip the hike and start at the beach. Picnic, play and leave the afternoon flexible. High Falls Gorge is an alternative main outing, not an obligation.
dayPlans.rain: In heavy rain, switch to the Lake Placid indoor plan.

dayPlans.name: Rainy Lake Placid: one anchor, one extra
dayPlans.plan: Start with the Olympic Museum and lunch. Choose either a confirmed public skating session or Big Z's afterward. A movie is an optional evening plan if the film and showtime fit.
dayPlans.rain: For toddlers, shorten the museum portion and prioritize play or a library stop.

dayPlans.name: Couples' foliage loop: Jay, Keene and the lakes
dayPlans.plan: Wilmington → Jay Covered Bridge → Upper Jay / Sugar House Creamery when open → Keene → Cascade Lakes picnic area → Lake Placid → Wilmington. Walk only as far as desired at each stop. Save Whiteface Memorial Highway for a separate clear-weather window.
dayPlans.rain: On a Sunday in season, add the Keene Farmers' Market and drop another stop.

dayPlans.name: Saranac Lake: choose boats or a small mountain
dayPlans.who: Families with school-age children; active couples
dayPlans.plan: Make either a Swiss Marine boat rental or Baker Mountain the anchor. Add a village meal; younger children may enjoy a short carousel visit. Donnelly's is a seasonal treat add-on only after confirming it is open.
dayPlans.rain: Use Saranac Laboratory Museum or a scheduled Pendragon performance for adults in poor weather.

dayPlans.name: Fit hikers: a full mountain day
dayPlans.plan: Choose Cascade or Giant, not both. Check conditions, arrange legal parking, start early, carry essentials and agree a turnaround time. Plan a simple meal afterward rather than another paid attraction.
dayPlans.rain: Choose a lower, shorter outing when weather or the group's energy is not suitable.

dayPlans.name: Quiet couple's day without a summit
dayPlans.who: Couples; visitors who prefer scenery and culture
dayPlans.plan: Start with Heaven Hill or a short Mirror Lake stroll. Choose a gallery visit or a prebooked spa treatment. Finish with dinner and, when scheduled, a Pendragon performance. Golf-oriented guests can swap the morning for Lake Placid Club.
dayPlans.rain: These are alternatives to customize, not four required bookings.

alerts.note: Private land: weekday hiking only; weekend parking and hiking prohibited. Recheck DEC and posted signs before every recommendation.
Operator homepage says the park is closed for the summer and fall seasons; winter start dates inconsistent. Confirm directly before publishing a holiday visit.
Lake Placid Marina explicitly says it is not operating boat tours or rentals. Captain Marney's is the Lake Placid rental recommendation.
Use 56 Woodruff Street, Saranac Lake. Do not route guests to the former Brandy Brook location.
Working farms are not visitor attractions: no petting zoo, tour or animal-feeding promise for Asgaard or Sugar House.
House canoe, kayak and inflatables: confirm availability, condition, life jackets and sizes, capacity, pickup/return and permitted use before publishing operational details.
Lake Placid's emergency room closed in August 2023. Never direct a guest to Lake Placid for emergency care; the nearest 24-hour ER is Saranac Lake.
Map apps (AllTrails, Gaia, Strava) may still show the old Mount Jo routing; ADK is correcting it. Follow signs on the ground.

places.name: Salt of the Earth Bistro
places.review: The strongest all-around food-first recommendation in the area. It is tiny (nine tables), intimate and chef-driven, with global flavors layered onto familiar dishes. Service is personal and the menu changes enough to reward repeat visits.
places.order: Follow the seasonal menu; duck, pork, salmon and unusual starters are recurring strengths.
places.knowBefore: Reservations are strongly encouraged; no children’s menu; not the choice for a fast or inexpensive dinner.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Reservations strongly encouraged
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Smoke Signals
places.review: One of the safest recommendations for visitors because it combines genuinely good barbecue, a lively bar and one of the better Mirror Lake deck settings. The huge review volume matters: this is a proven crowd-pleaser, not a tiny high-rated outlier.
places.order: Brisket, smoked wings, BBQ plates and loaded starters.
places.knowBefore: Peak dinner times can mean waits. Ask for the deck when weather cooperates.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Walk-in; expect waits at peak
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Caffè Rustica
places.review: A food-driven choice away from the Main Street tourist strip. The room is small and cozy, the cooking leans Italian/Mediterranean, and it is a strong alternative when you want a real dinner without the downtown scene.
places.order: Wood-fired pizza, seafood, veal/short-rib style specials and tiramisu.
places.knowBefore: Limited seating makes reservations important; seasonal specials can differ from online menus.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Reservations important
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Lisa G's
places.review: A fun, energetic local favorite that does comfort food with more personality than a standard pub. The menu has enough variety for a mixed group, and the patio/deck is a major plus.
places.order: Wings, calamari, creative appetizers, fish-and-fries and rotating comfort-food specials.
places.knowBefore: Can be loud and busy; service pacing varies at peak times. Reservations are smart.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Reservations smart
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Top of the Park
places.review: The recommendation here is experience-first: creative cocktails, a spectacular Mirror Lake vantage point and polished small plates. It is excellent when you want to linger rather than simply eat a large dinner.
places.order: A signature cocktail plus several small plates to share.
places.knowBefore: Portions are intentionally small and prices can feel premium. Treat it as tapas, not a steakhouse.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Heritage Indian Grill
places.address: 45 Hadjis Way, Suite 6, Lake Placid, NY 12946
places.review: One of the most useful “change of pace” restaurants in Lake Placid. It has a modern interior, a broad menu, strong vegetarian choices and flavors that stand apart from the area’s burger/BBQ concentration.
places.order: Butter chicken, tikka masala, tandoori items, biryani, chana masala and garlic naan.
places.knowBefore: Medium spice can run hot; service can slow when the room is slammed.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Big Mountain Deli & Crêperie
places.review: A very good daytime answer when you want something fast but not generic. The enormous sandwich/crêpe menu and central location make it especially useful before or after outdoor activities.
places.order: One of the “46” sandwiches, a savory crêpe or a sweet crêpe to share.
places.knowBefore: Small dining room and lots of choices; takeout or ordering ahead can be easier at rush hour.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Order ahead at rush hour
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Jimmy's 21 Lake Side Italian Restaurant
places.review: A classic, old-school Lake Placid option with a very good setting and a broad Italian-American menu. It is especially appealing to groups who want familiar food and a lake view rather than adventurous cooking.
places.order: Homemade pasta dishes, seafood, chicken/veal classics and steak.
places.knowBefore: Reviews are less consistent than the top tier; you are partly paying for location and atmosphere.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Country Bear Restaurant
places.review: The best breakfast-specific recommendation in Wilmington. It is tiny, unfussy and beloved for exactly what it is: a classic mountain-town diner serving hearty breakfast without tourist polish.
places.order: French toast, pancakes, eggs/home fries and homemade breads or muffins.
places.knowBefore: Cash-only is commonly reported; hours are limited and waits can build quickly.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: The Hungry Trout Restaurant
places.review: The best Wilmington answer when you want a more complete sit-down dinner rather than pub food. Its long association with the Ausable River and Whiteface area gives it a classic Adirondack feel.
places.order: Trout and other fish preparations, steak and seasonal Adirondack-style entrées.
places.knowBefore: Hours and restaurant concepts can be seasonal; verify before driving.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Reservations advised

places.name: Twisted Raven
places.review: A lively local hangout at the base of Whiteface Memorial Highway. The draw is generous pub food, events and a relaxed bar atmosphere rather than refined dining.
places.order: Burgers, wings, smoked foods, fries and pub specials.
places.knowBefore: Can get busy around events; expect a pub pace, not fine-dining service.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: Up a Creek Restaurant
places.review: A solid, no-drama local choice when convenience and comfort food matter more than destination dining. It fills the “easy breakfast or casual meal” role well in Wilmington.
places.order: Stuffed French toast, pancakes and other breakfast/comfort-food specials.
places.knowBefore: Not a special-occasion restaurant; hours can be seasonal, so check first.
places.season: Hours can be seasonal — check first
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: Our Plates | Pan-Caribbean
places.review: One of the most distinctive meals in the whole three-town area. It is owner-driven, flavor-forward and refreshingly different from the Adirondacks’ dominant pub/steak/Italian mix.
places.order: Cubano, jerk or stewed chicken, tostones and empanadas.
places.knowBefore: Smaller operation; menu and hours may shift, so confirm before a dedicated drive.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Confirm hours before a dedicated drive

places.name: Red Fox Restaurant
places.review: A dependable traditional dinner with a loyal following. Red Fox is the recommendation when someone wants a real steak-and-seafood meal, generous portions and old-school hospitality rather than a trendy concept.
places.order: Prime rib, steaks, seafood and Italian-American classics.
places.knowBefore: Prime rib can sell out; reservations are a good idea on busy nights.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive
places.booking: Reservations on busy nights

places.name: RiverTrail Beerworks
places.review: A very strong modern-casual option: riverfront setting, good beer, pizza and plenty of room to socialize. It is especially useful for mixed-age groups or a low-pressure evening.
places.order: Detroit-style pizza, brewpub snacks and house beer.
places.knowBefore: Weekend crowds can slow things down; go for the total brewpub experience rather than culinary formality.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: Bitters & Bones
places.review: A polished but still casual downtown tavern with more energy than a standard brewpub. It works especially well for adults who want good drinks and enough food variety to stay for dinner.
places.order: Burgers, tacos, fry plates, rotating pub dishes and house beer/cocktails.
places.knowBefore: Can be loud and social; not the first choice for a quiet romantic meal.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: Blue Moon Café
places.review: A reliable Saranac Lake breakfast institution with enough review volume to make it a safe bet. It is not fancy; it is the kind of place you use repeatedly during a stay.
places.order: Corned beef hash, eggs, pancakes and house-baked breads/English muffins.
places.knowBefore: Popular breakfast hours bring waits. Go early if you have a schedule.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: Donnelly's Soft Ice Cream
places.review: A genuine must-stop, not merely “good ice cream.” The soft serve is exceptionally light and creamy, and the one-flavor-per-day ritual is part of the tradition. It is worth a short detour even if you are staying in Lake Placid.
places.order: Whatever the flavor of the day is, twisted with vanilla. That is essentially the point.
places.knowBefore: Seasonal, typically Memorial Day through Labor Day, and cash-only is commonly reported. Check the daily flavor and opening status before driving.
places.season: Seasonal — typically Memorial Day to Labor Day
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: Tail O' the Pup
places.subcategory: Seasonal outdoor BBQ / seafood / live music
places.review: Go for the experience as much as the food: picnic-table dining under the pines, live music, kids running around and an unmistakably Adirondack summer-roadside atmosphere. The Google score is notably lower than the top food destinations, and reviews show real inconsistency, so it should not be sold as the area’s best barbecue on food alone.
places.order: BBQ staples, clam chowder, lobster/seafood and cornbread when available.
places.knowBefore: Service and food execution can be uneven when busy. Seasonal (roughly May–October); check hours and arrive with a relaxed schedule.
places.hours: Verify same-day hours before a long drive

places.name: Whiteface Mountain
places.review: The Olympic mountain, with the greatest vertical drop in the East. The reason most winter guests come to Wilmington.
places.season: Winter alpine season; summer gondola rides
places.booking: Lift tickets sold online; verify current pass options

places.name: Mt Van Hoevenberg (Nordic)
places.review: Cross-country trails, biathlon range and the bobsled track on the same site.
places.booking: Day passes; rentals on site — verify
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Whiteface via the Wilmington Trail
places.review: A full-day climb from the Wilmington side to the summit. Long, steep, and worth every step on a clear day.
places.season: Summer and autumn; winter for equipped hikers only
places.booking: None

places.name: Cooper Kiln Pond
places.review: A quieter walk to a backcountry pond on the shoulder of Whiteface.
places.booking: None

places.name: Copperas Pond: direct northern approach
places.review: A short, steep woodland approach to a peaceful mountain pond. A good family outing when children already handle roots and uphill walking.
places.knowBefore: Roughly one mile round trip from the direct northern Route 86 trailhead. It is not the longer Owen–Copperas–Winch itinerary. Follow the marked route and avoid turning a short visit into an unplanned road walk.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

places.fitness: Basic-to-moderate fitness with sure footing; about 450 feet of climbing is concentrated into a short approach.
places.children: Better for capable school-age walkers than toddlers. Close supervision near the water; no stroller.
places.payoff: A quiet pond, mountain backdrop and reflective water rather than a summit.

places.name: Flume Trails
places.review: Wilmington's mountain-bike network, built for it. Rentals in town — verify which shops currently operate.
places.booking: None

source.name: Barkeater Trails Alliance / Town of Wilmington

places.name: Hardy Road Trails
places.review: A second local network with a different character to the Flume.
places.booking: None

places.name: West Branch of the Ausable River
places.review: One of the most famous trout rivers in the Northeast runs through the village. Guides are worth it if you are new to it.
places.season: Verify current regulations and catch-and-release sections
places.booking: NYS fishing licence

places.name: Whiteface Veterans' Memorial Highway
places.address: Whiteface Veterans' Memorial Highway, Wilmington, NY 12997
places.review: A mountain drive to the castle area, followed by summit access using the elevator when available or the rocky stair route. The drive itself is part of the attraction. First choice for a major mountain view without a long hike. Choose a clear day rather than spending the admission budget to drive into cloud.
places.knowBefore: The drive estimate is to the highway entrance, not the summit. The summit stair route is uneven and strenuous for some guests; confirm elevator operation for mobility needs. Seasonal and weather closures apply; the 2026 planned closing date is October 12, subject to conditions.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: High Falls Gorge
places.review: Managed walkways and bridges bring visitors close to a series of four waterfalls. It delivers a substantial scenic experience without committing to a mountain hike. Allow longer than the operator's shortest advertised walking time for photos and children.
places.knowBefore: Expect steps and wet surfaces on the full experience. Do not assume every section is stroller- or wheelchair-accessible. Check seasonal closure dates; light drizzle may be workable, but storms or heavy rain are not a reason to seek out a gorge.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Ausable Chasm
places.review: A dramatic sandstone gorge with walking routes and separately selected river or adventure experiences. Choose the package around the least adventurous person, not the most adventurous. Best as a main attraction for the day.
places.knowBefore: Gorge routes involve stairs and uneven ground. Rafting, tubing and adventure courses have different age, size and water-condition requirements; do not assume one ticket or one eligibility rule covers everything. Confirm restrictions when booking.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Lake Placid & the Olympic sites
places.review: Main Street, Mirror Lake and the Olympic venues from 1932 and 1980.
places.booking: Site passes — verify
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: Jay Covered Bridge / Douglas Memorial Park
places.review: A covered bridge, riverside setting and picnic space that work well for guests who want scenery without a long walk. An easy local recommendation and a natural starting point for a Jay / Upper Jay foliage loop.
places.knowBefore: Enjoy the river from public paths and viewing areas. The rocks and river are not a recommended swimming or cliff-jumping location. Surfaces and seasonal facilities vary.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Santa's Workshop
places.review: A small, old-fashioned theme park that has been here since 1949.
places.knowBefore: The operator homepage says the park is closed for the summer and fall operating seasons; winter notices show inconsistent start dates. Confirm directly before promising a holiday visit.
places.booking: Verify

places.name: Adirondack Wildlife Refuge
places.review: Wolves, raptors and rehabilitation animals. Check current opening before you go.
places.booking: Verify

places.name: Lake Placid Olympic Museum
places.review: Indoor exhibits about Lake Placid's Olympic history, including the 1932 and 1980 Winter Games. The best straightforward museum anchor for a rainy Lake Placid day. Combine it with lunch and one other activity.
places.knowBefore: Check current hours and tickets. The museum and public skating are separate plans within the Olympic Center; access to one does not establish availability of the other.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: The Wild Center
places.review: A substantial indoor natural-history experience with hands-on exhibits and live animals. The outdoor Wild Walk adds a separate treetop experience when conditions allow. The strongest farther-away family museum option; make it the main outing.
places.knowBefore: Reserve or check entry availability and seasonal hours. Indoor exhibits work for a rainy day; Wild Walk, trails and other outdoor installations remain weather-dependent. The longer drive is part of the decision.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Nearest hospitals
places.review: Adirondack Medical Center sites in Lake Placid and Saranac Lake, and Elizabethtown Community Hospital. Confirm which has 24-hour emergency care before publishing.

places.review: Licensed local guides for the West Branch. Names are listed only after verification; this may link to RŌM or other approved providers.

places.review: Nearest full grocery, pharmacy, hardware and fuel will be listed with drive times once verified.

places.name: Emergency: 911
places.review: Fire, police and ambulance. The property's posted instructions and the local responder's number are provided privately with your arrival details, never on this public page.
places.knowBefore: Give the property's address from your arrival details. Cell coverage is patchy in the Notch and on trails.

places.name: Heaven Hill: Big Field Loop
places.review: A short meadow-and-woods outing rather than a mountain climb. The Big Field Loop is the best starting point for children who want to explore at their own pace; do not confuse it with the longer trail network.
places.knowBefore: Use the trailhead map to stay on the 0.9-mile Big Field Loop. Wet ground and uneven surfaces can occur; this is not a guaranteed smooth stroller route.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

places.fitness: Basic walking ability on a natural path. Ideal when the group has mixed stamina or wants frequent stops.
places.children: Top choice for preschoolers and young walkers. Let the shortest-legged person set the pace; bring a carrier when needed.
places.payoff: Open High Peaks views without having to climb a High Peak.

places.name: Cobble Lookout
places.review: The best nearby view-to-effort choice for a family that can manage a couple of miles. A gently rolling forest trail reaches a broad open lookout over the valley and surrounding mountains.
places.knowBefore: Trailhead is on Gillespie Drive / County Route 18A near Whiteface Memorial Highway. The published route is about 2.4 miles; some maps round it differently. Not stroller-friendly.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

places.fitness: Comfort walking two-plus miles on roots, rocks and occasional mud. Much less climbing than a summit hike, but still a real trail.
places.children: Good for capable younger children with patient adults; toddlers may need a carrier. Hold small children close at the unguarded lookout and stay well back from the edge.
places.payoff: A big Adirondack panorama for comparatively little climbing.

places.name: Brewster Peninsula: short lake-and-woods walk
places.review: A flexible network of short woodland trails beside Lake Placid. Choose a small out-and-back or linked loop rather than feeling obliged to complete every trail.
places.knowBefore: The suggested 1–2 miles is a selected outing, not the official length of the whole network. Consult the junction map; the Lakeshore Trail is rockier than the gentler interior sections.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Basic walking stamina with enough balance for roots and uneven lakeside rock.
places.children: Good for younger children who enjoy woods and water. The shoreline requires close supervision; a carrier is more useful than a stroller.
places.payoff: A real lakeshore outing with forest shade and water views, close to the village.

places.name: Mirror Lake village loop
places.review: A paved village walk around Mirror Lake, not a wilderness hike. Shops and lake views make it easy to turn a walk into a relaxed morning or afternoon.
places.knowBefore: Allow extra time for stops and parking. Follow sidewalks and crossings; a paved route is not a promise of step-free access at every business or side path.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Comfortable walking on pavement; shorten it to an out-and-back whenever the group has had enough.
places.children: Good for all ages with adult supervision at road crossings. The most practical core choice for a stroller; benches and shorter turnaround options help mixed-mobility groups.
places.payoff: Lake reflections, mountain backdrops and easy access to the village.

places.name: Bloomingdale Bog: short out-and-back
places.review: A nearly level former rail corridor through an unusual wetland landscape. Choose a turnaround point based on the group rather than aiming for the full trail.
places.knowBefore: The full trail is approximately 3.7 miles one way; this recommendation is only a 1–3-mile total outing. Northern access is generally the better stroller choice. Beaver flooding can affect the southern portion.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

places.fitness: Basic walking fitness. The main challenge is distance, not climbing.
places.children: Suitable for children who enjoy birds, plants and a quiet nature walk. Bring insect protection in season and supervise near water or flooded sections.
places.payoff: Wide-open bog scenery and a different Adirondack habitat from the mountain trails.

places.name: Paul Smith's VIC: Barnum Brook Trail
places.review: A short interpretive nature walk at the Paul Smith's College Visitor Interpretive Center. A worthwhile farther-afield outing for guests who prefer nature observation over climbing.
places.knowBefore: The selected trail is 0.6 mile, not the larger VIC network. Check lodge hours and seasonal programs; the butterfly house is a seasonal, weather-dependent extra, not a guaranteed indoor rainy-day attraction.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Low exertion. The college describes Barnum Brook as ADA-accessible; confirm current surface and access conditions for specific mobility needs.
places.children: Good for young children and multigenerational groups. The visitor center makes it easier to pair a small walk with a longer nature-focused visit.
places.payoff: Marsh, forest and water-level scenery in a compact outing.

places.name: Mount Jo via the Long Trail
places.review: A classic small mountain with a much bigger view than its size suggests. The Long Trail is the preferred family approach, but roots, rocks and sustained climbing keep this out of the toddler-stroll category.
places.knowBefore: Start at the Adirondak Loj / Heart Lake trailhead. Allow for paid parking and busy weekends. About 2.6 miles round trip via the Long Trail; the shorter route is steeper, not automatically easier. Apps may still show the old routing — ADK is correcting it.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Moderate fitness and comfort walking uphill on uneven ground; the descent still takes concentration.
places.children: Best for school-age children who already manage rocky hikes. A fit adult with a carrier may choose it, but carrying a child does not make the footing easier.
places.payoff: Heart Lake framed by major High Peaks: one of the strongest shorter-hike payoffs.

places.name: Baker Mountain
places.review: A compact climb above Saranac Lake with a substantial amount of uphill packed into a short distance. Convenient for pairing a hike with a village visit.
places.knowBefore: Use the Moody Pond trailhead and respect the residential neighborhood and posted parking. Published mileage varies slightly with starting point; this guide uses the regional 1.6-mile round trip.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Moderate fitness, steady uphill effort and confidence descending rocks and roots.
places.children: Good for capable school-age children who like a summit goal. Not an effortless walk simply because it is under two miles.
places.payoff: Views over Saranac Lake, Lake Flower and surrounding mountains.

places.name: Mt Van Hoevenberg: East Trail
places.review: A purpose-built mountain trail with extensive stonework and a summit ledge looking toward the High Peaks. A strong option for active families who want a proper half-day hike.
places.knowBefore: This entry is specifically the East Trail from the Mountain Pass Lodge area, not the West Trail. The regional guide lists 3.6 miles round trip. Check venue access, parking and current trail information before leaving.

places.booking: None

places.fitness: Moderate fitness with the ability to handle about 1,000 feet of climbing and many uneven steps.
places.children: Best for school-age children with established hiking stamina. Keep children well back from the exposed summit edge.
places.payoff: Expansive High Peaks views and an attractive, deliberately built trail.

places.name: Cascade Mountain from Route 73
places.review: A genuine Adirondack High Peak and a reasonable first choice for a fit, prepared mountain hiker. The rocky ascent ends on an exposed summit; “one of the easier High Peaks” does not mean easy.
places.knowBefore: This distance is for the Route 73 route, without adding Porter. Parking fills early and no-parking zones are enforced. Check DEC for current access and conditions; do not improvise roadside parking.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Strong day-hiking fitness, sustained uphill ability and stable footing on rock. Be prepared for a demanding descent and rapidly changing summit weather.
places.children: Only for children or teenagers who already hike comparable terrain and distance. Not a default family outing or first mountain walk.
places.payoff: A broad, above-treeline panorama and a true High Peak summit.

places.name: Jay Mountain: first summit
places.review: A substantial climb to an open ridge with a less crowded-feeling, rugged mountain setting. The recommended turnaround is the first summit at the end of the marked trail, not an automatic traverse of the entire ridge.
places.knowBefore: The true summit extension is about 7.3 miles round trip with roughly 2,675 feet of gain; beyond the marked route, navigation and slab travel are more demanding. Jay is not one of the 46 High Peaks. Use the western trailhead near Jay Mountain Road and Upland Meadows Road.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

links.label: Regional guide: first summit and longer ridge option

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Strong hiking fitness and comfort on exposed rock. Ridge travel requires particular care in wind, rain and poor visibility.
places.children: Experienced hiking families with older children or teenagers only. Not a small-child recommendation.
places.payoff: Open ridgeline views and a distinctive mountain landscape close to Wilmington.

places.name: Giant Mountain: Ridge / Zander Scott Trail
places.review: A steep, sustained climb with open rock, large views and a serious physical commitment. The mileage looks modest beside the amount of elevation gained.
places.knowBefore: This is the Ridge / Zander Scott route from Route 73, approximately 5.4 miles round trip with 3,050 feet of gain. Do not substitute Roaring Brook route statistics. Start early and allow more than eight hours for a slower party.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Very good mountain-hiking fitness, strong legs and experience with steep rock on both ascent and descent. This is the hardest core recommendation.
places.children: Experienced, fit older teenagers and adults are the best match. Not a general family hike and not the place to test whether a child enjoys mountains.
places.payoff: A major High Peak summit with dramatic views and frequent scenery along the climb.

places.name: Owls Head in Keene: weekdays only
places.review: A short climb with scrambling and open ledges. Its small distance is appealing, but it needs a more careful family suitability label than “easy for everyone.”
places.knowBefore: Private land: DEC currently permits weekday hiking only; weekend hiking and parking are prohibited. Follow posted restrictions. This is Keene's Owls Head, not Owl Head Lookout in Giant Mountain Wilderness or the Long Lake mountain.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Basic-to-moderate fitness and confidence on uneven rock; hands may be useful on steeper sections.
places.children: Capable school-age children with close adult supervision. Not a stroller walk, and exposed edges make it a poor default for toddlers.
places.payoff: A rewarding mountain view from a relatively short outing.

places.name: Hurricane Mountain from Route 9N
places.review: A full mountain day with a fire tower and broad views, useful for fit guests who want an alternative to a 46er.
places.knowBefore: The Route 9N approach is 6.8 miles round trip, not the shorter alternative from another trailhead. Check DEC tower and trail notices. Not one of the 46 High Peaks.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Strong day-hiking fitness and several hours of uphill and downhill stamina.
places.children: Experienced older children or teenagers only; no need to climb the tower to enjoy the summit landscape.
places.payoff: An open summit and fire-tower setting with wide-ranging views.

places.name: Ampersand Mountain
places.review: A Saranac Lake-area mountain hike that becomes markedly steeper on the upper climb. It belongs with the strenuous options despite its popularity.
places.knowBefore: Plan for 5.4 miles round trip and approximately 1,780 feet of climbing. The upper rock can be slippery when wet. Not one of the 46 High Peaks.
places.season: Snow-free, reasonably dry conditions assumed; check DEC notices
places.booking: None

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.fitness: Good mountain-hiking fitness and confidence descending steep rock.
places.children: Experienced hiking children or teenagers only; keep the group back from summit drops.
places.payoff: A broad open summit with lakes and mountains in nearly every direction.

places.name: Wilmington Town Beach / Lake Everest
places.review: A sandy beach, playground, picnic space and a peaceful water setting make this the easiest family recommendation close to the house. Best for an unhurried beach-and-picnic day, or a low-effort afternoon after a morning hike.
places.knowBefore: Swimming and public rentals depend on seasonal operations and staffing. Confirm the beach is open; being able to enter the park is not the same as having lifeguarded swimming. Ask us in advance about the canoe, kayak and inflatables kept at the house.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Cloudsplitter Gondola at Whiteface
places.review: A gondola ride from Whiteface's ski area to the Little Whiteface observation area. A different outing from the Memorial Highway. A strong choice for groups that enjoy a ride and a mountain view but are not looking for a summit hike.
bestFor: visitors who want elevation without hiking
places.knowBefore: The gondola goes to Little Whiteface, not Whiteface Mountain's actual summit. Check operating days, weather, wind restrictions and current accessibility before setting out.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Olympic Jumping Complex Skyride
places.review: A gondola and elevator visit to the ski-jump observation area, with a close look at the scale of Olympic ski jumping. A compact attraction with a strong visual payoff, especially for guests interested in the Olympic story but not a full museum visit.
places.knowBefore: Use current visitor directions and the designated parking area. Confirm weather and operating schedules. The Skyride is different from the separately operated zipline or event admission.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Cliffside Coaster at Mt Van Hoevenberg
places.address: Mt Van Hoevenberg, 220 Bobsled Run Lane, Lake Placid, NY 12946
places.review: A mountain coaster near the Olympic sliding facilities. A useful change of pace from hiking and sightseeing. Best for children and adults who enjoy rides. Check eligibility before mentioning it to a child as a definite plan.
places.knowBefore: Age, height and combined rider-weight rules apply. The operator currently requires solo drivers to be at least nine and 52 inches tall; carrying a passenger requires an adult driver and additional passenger rules. Book the appropriate slot and recheck all restrictions and weather operations.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Swiss Marine / Swiss Boat Rentals
places.review: Our preferred Saranac Lake rental. The operator lists pontoon, fishing and ski boats, so the outing can suit a relaxed cruise or a more active day. Treat boating as the main activity, with a village stop afterward rather than an overloaded schedule.
bestFor: multigenerational groups able to board a boat
places.knowBefore: Call to confirm the exact boat and seating configuration, launch location, permitted route, operator qualifications, child life jackets, fuel, deposits and weather cancellation terms. Mobility-friendly boarding should be verified, not assumed.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Captain Marney's Boat Rental
places.address: Multiple Lake Placid locations; confirm pickup when booking
places.review: Our preferred Lake Placid boat rental. Its fleet includes pontoon boats, bowriders and deck boats. Choose a relaxed lake cruise for mixed-age groups and confirm the most appropriate boat for everyone's comfort.
places.knowBefore: Book by phone. The operator lists multiple pickup locations, so confirm the meeting point rather than relying on a generic map pin. Verify payment method, qualifications, life jackets, fuel and weather terms. This is on Lake Placid, not the smaller downtown Mirror Lake.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Boots and Birdies
places.review: Outdoor miniature golf, with additional activities such as batting cages and gem mining listed by the operator. A good option when children have had enough scenery and want to play.
places.knowBefore: Seasonal and weather-dependent. It is not the rainy-day arcade recommendation; that role belongs to Big Z's.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Adirondack Rail Trail: selected out-and-back
places.area: Lake Placid / Ray Brook / Saranac Lake
places.address: Choose a current official access point in Lake Placid, Ray Brook or Saranac Lake
places.review: A largely gentle, compacted-surface rail corridor that allows a short walk or bike ride instead of a full mountain-bike experience. Choose a 2–6-mile total out-and-back appropriate to the group.
bestFor: Families who can walk or ride predictably
places.knowBefore: A shared trail, not a closed children's play area. Use helmets for cycling, maintain control and supervise road crossings. Check DEC construction, access and parking updates before choosing a trailhead; conditions and facilities vary by segment.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Public ice skating at the Olympic Center
places.review: A memorable way to experience an Olympic venue while staying indoors. A top rainy-day activity when the public-session calendar works. Particularly useful for children who need to move after a museum visit.
bestFor: couples comfortable trying an ice activity
places.knowBefore: Confirm an actual public skating session, available rental sizes and any age or equipment rules. A practice session or event on the calendar is not necessarily public skating. Pack warm layers.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Big Z's at Lake Placid Lanes
places.review: Bowling and arcade games in the same venue, with casual food available. The best all-purpose rainy-day play option for a group that does not want another museum.
places.knowBefore: Call about lanes, busy periods and current hours. Use the current Big Z's name rather than an old Bowlwinkles listing.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Adirondack Carousel
places.review: An enclosed carousel featuring carved Adirondack wildlife rather than a standard set of horses. A particularly good small-child rainy-day stop. Pair it with a meal or another Saranac Lake activity; it is not a full-day attraction.
places.knowBefore: Check the seasonal operating schedule before promising a ride. Ask about accessibility needs and current ride arrangements.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Lake Placid Public Library
places.review: A village library with reading space and a program calendar. A useful modest option when the group needs a break rather than another ticketed attraction.
places.knowBefore: Check opening hours and the actual program calendar; accompany children. Borrowing privileges or program registration need to be confirmed with the library.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Palace Theatre
places.review: A classic village movie theater, useful for a wet evening or a scheduled matinee. A strong backup when the current film appeals to the group.
places.knowBefore: Check today's film and showtimes. The regional listing says cash only and no advance tickets; confirm before visiting.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Lake Placid Center for the Arts / Gallery 46
places.address: Arts center: 17 Algonquin Drive; Gallery 46: 2525 Main Street, Lake Placid, NY
places.review: Gallery browsing, performances and classes offer a quieter alternative to the sports attractions. Gallery 46 is downtown; the arts center campus is a separate location.
bestFor: families when a suitable program is scheduled
places.knowBefore: Check exhibition hours, performance dates, class registration and age suitability. Do not assume a drop-in children's art session is available every rainy day.
places.cost: Gallery browsing or ticket / class fee
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Pendragon Theatre
places.review: Live theater in its new downtown Saranac Lake home, a good evening anchor for guests who want more than dining and a scenic drive.
bestFor: families only when the production fits
places.knowBefore: The current address is 56 Woodruff Street, not the former Brandy Brook location. Check the production, content suitability and exact date, and reserve seats.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Saranac Laboratory Museum
places.review: A smaller museum exploring Saranac Lake's medical and tuberculosis-treatment history. A distinctive rainy-day choice for curious adults.
places.knowBefore: Check current museum hours. Best for older children who enjoy history; not a substitute for the Wild Center's hands-on family scale.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Spa at Mirror Lake Inn
places.address: 77 Mirror Lake Drive, Lake Placid, NY 12946
places.review: A treatment-based spa option for a quieter, higher-budget rainy day. A good adult alternative to bowling or a museum when relaxation is the point of the trip.
places.knowBefore: Book ahead and confirm that non-hotel guests can reserve the desired service. A treatment booking does not include hotel pool, beach or other resort access. Policies and age limits apply.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: John Brown Farm State Historic Site
places.address: 115 John Brown Road, Lake Placid, NY 12946
places.review: A historic home, burial site and grounds associated with abolitionist John Brown. A history recommendation, not a petting farm. A useful way to add substance to a relaxed Lake Placid day.
places.knowBefore: Grounds access and indoor house or barn opening schedules differ by season. Confirm tours and hours. Only the open indoor portions belong in a rainy-day plan.
places.cost: Low-cost heritage visit; verify tour details
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Sugar House Creamery
places.address: 18 Sugar House Way, Upper Jay, NY 12987
places.review: A working farm and cheese-focused farm store in Upper Jay. It fits naturally into a relaxed loop through Jay and Keene. A small, characterful stop for local food, not a large organized farm attraction.
places.knowBefore: Check opening days before driving over. Do not expect a tour, animal feeding, petting access or a view of production. Respect the working farm and private areas.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Asgaard Farm & Dairy: farm-store visit
places.address: 74 Asgaard Way, Au Sable Forks, NY 12912
places.review: A working-farm store stop that can add local character to a Jay / Au Sable Forks outing. A secondary recommendation rather than a structured animal attraction.
places.knowBefore: Online descriptions of current dairy operations and products are inconsistent. Call to confirm the store's days, products and any permitted visitor activities. No goat-dairy tour or petting zoo is promised.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Keene Farmers' Market at Marcy Field
places.review: An outdoor farmers' market in a scenic valley setting. A good reason to make a Sunday drive toward Keene. Pair it with a picnic or another easy scenic stop.
places.knowBefore: The published 2026 schedule is Sundays, May 24 through October 11, 9 a.m.–2 p.m. Recheck for future seasons and special changes. An outdoor market, not an indoor rainy-day attraction.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Lake Placid Club Golf Courses
places.review: Our clear first golf recommendation. The property offers the 18-hole Links and Mountain courses plus the shorter Pristine 9. For a mixed-ability family or a shorter afternoon, ask about the Pristine 9 rather than committing everyone to 18 holes.
places.knowBefore: Allow roughly 1.5–2.5 hours for a short nine-hole outing and 4–5 hours for 18 holes. Confirm course choice, tee times, rental clubs, cart policies and seasonal conditions.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Craig Wood Golf Course
places.address: 141 Country Club Road, Lake Placid, NY 12946
places.review: A public municipal golf alternative outside the village. Second choice after the Lake Placid Club, useful when preferred tee times are unavailable. This order reflects our preference, not an independently scored ranking.
bestFor: Golfers seeking a backup tee time or different setting
places.knowBefore: Call or book online for current tee times, rates, rental equipment and course conditions. Golf is not a rainy-day fallback during storms.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Saranac Inn Golf & Country Club
places.review: An 18-hole course in the Upper Saranac Lake area, best treated as a golf-focused outing rather than a quick village add-on.
bestFor: Golfers willing to drive farther for a different course
places.knowBefore: Confirm tee times and seasonal operations. This is Saranac Inn Golf & Country Club, not the similarly named Saranac Lake Golf Club in Ray Brook.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

source.name: Wilmington Adirondack Hikes & Activities Guide 2026 (owner research)

places.name: Cascade Lakes picnic area
places.address: Cascade Lakes picnic area between Upper and Lower Cascade Lakes, Route 73, NY
places.review: The small picnic area between Upper and Lower Cascade Lakes offers water-level mountain scenery without a summit climb. One of our strongest low-effort recommendations. Bring a picnic and enjoy the reflections.
places.knowBefore: Parking is limited. Use the designated area and do not stop unsafely along Route 73. This is for the picnic and lake view, not a scramble to the waterfall or slide. Verify ground conditions for mobility needs.
places.booking: Check operator schedule; book where noted

places.name: Wilmington Fire & Rescue
places.review: All-volunteer fire and ambulance service for the town, 24/7/365. Dial 911 for any emergency; this number is for non-emergency questions only.
places.knowBefore: Non-emergency line only. In an emergency call 911.

places.name: Adirondack Medical Center — Saranac Lake (24-hour ER)
places.review: The nearest 24-hour emergency department to Wilmington, about 35 minutes west on NY-86. Lake Placid no longer has an emergency room: it closed in August 2023.
places.knowBefore: Roughly 35 minutes by car in normal conditions. For life-threatening emergencies call 911 rather than driving.

places.name: UVM Health — Elizabethtown Community Hospital (24-hour ER)
places.review: A critical-access hospital with a 24/7 emergency department, roughly 40 minutes southeast via Jay and Route 9N. An alternative to Saranac Lake depending on where you are.
places.knowBefore: Confirm the direct ED phone and street address before publishing; search results returned only a PO box.

places.name: UVM Health — CVPH Medical Center, Plattsburgh (trauma center)
places.review: The regional Level III trauma center, about an hour northeast. Where serious injuries are likely to be taken.
places.knowBefore: Confirm the main phone number before publishing.

places.name: NYS DEC Forest Rangers (backcountry emergency)
places.review: For a lost or injured hiker, a wildfire, or an emergency on state land. Call 911 and ask for Forest Ranger assistance, or call DEC dispatch directly.
places.knowBefore: Save the number before a hike. Cell coverage is unreliable on most trails; tell someone your route and turnaround time.

places.name: New York State Police — Troop B, Ray Brook
places.review: State Police headquarters for the North Country, covering Essex County. Non-emergency line.
places.knowBefore: Emergencies: 911.

places.name: Essex County Sheriff's Office
places.review: County law enforcement, non-emergency line.
places.knowBefore: Emergencies: 911.

places.name: Poison Control
places.review: Free, confidential, 24 hours. For a suspected poisoning, medication mix-up or a child who has swallowed something.
places.knowBefore: If the person is unconscious or not breathing, call 911.

places.name: Adirondack Health — Lake Placid Health Center (weekday urgent care)
places.address: 203 Old Military Road, Lake Placid, NY 12946
places.review: Primary and urgent care Monday–Friday 8:30–5:00; urgent care after 5 p.m. by request. Not an emergency room.
places.knowBefore: For anything serious after hours, the 24-hour ER is in Saranac Lake.
places.drive: 15 min down the road · 13 mi via NY-86

places.name: VCA High Peaks Animal Hospital (veterinarian)
places.review: Nearest veterinary hospital on the road to Saranac Lake. Call ahead; confirm emergency availability.
places.knowBefore: Pet policy for the property is still pending; this is for guests travelling with an approved animal.

places.name: Town of Wilmington offices
places.review: Town hall: parks and beach operations, local questions.
places.knowBefore: Business hours only.

places.name: Kinney Drugs — Lake Placid (pharmacy)
places.review: Nearest full pharmacy, about 20 minutes away. Store and pharmacy hours differ; the pharmacy closes for lunch.

places.name: Wilmington: fuel, basics and local shops
places.review: Nearest fuel, convenience basics, ATM, hardware and local shops in Wilmington itself. To be listed by name after the owner confirms which are currently operating.

places.name: Noon Mark Diner
places.review: A small-town diner on Route 73 in Keene Valley, known far beyond the valley for its pies. The breakfast stop when your day is heading toward Cascade, Giant or the Keene side.
bestFor: Breakfast on a Keene or Keene Valley day
places.order: Pancakes or eggs, then a slice of pie to take away.
places.knowBefore: Small and busy on hiking mornings; hours vary by season — confirm. The owner remembers this as “the little diner in Keene”; confirm it is the right place.

places.name: Lake Placid Pub & Brewery
places.address: 813 Mirror Lake Drive, Lake Placid, NY 12946
places.review: The village brewpub above Mirror Lake and the home of Ubu Ale. Casual, loud in a good way, and easy with a group.
places.order: Ubu Ale, a flight, pub food.

places.name: Big Slide Brewery & Public House
places.review: A newer brewery on the edge of the village with a proper kitchen and wood-fired pizza. The pick when the beer matters as much as dinner.

places.review: Main Street brewery and steakhouse in one, with a patio on the street. Dependable for a mixed group.

places.name: Ausable Brewing Company
places.review: A farm brewery on the Ausable outside Keeseville: outdoor tables, food trucks, live music in summer. Pairs naturally with an Ausable Chasm day.
